column1: asset-owner|A|A3|crest|A client lists an IP owned by a supplier but cannot describe the service agreement. What should scoping establish?|The authority and conditions for testing that supplier-hosted asset|Only that the IP responds to a TCP probe|Only the client's corporate registration number|Only that the supplier uses the same country code|Technical reachability and a client's request do not settle third-party testing authority. Resolve ownership and applicable permission boundaries.|The asset's relationship to the client must be documented.

objective-method|A|A3|crest|A client asks whether one business function resists account takeover. What should primarily shape the test plan?|The function's authentication and recovery paths|A fixed scan of every Internet port|The tester's preferred exploit framework alone|Only the number of public website images|Client objectives determine relevant paths, identities, and depth. Broad discovery can support the objective without replacing it.|Tools should serve the question the client needs answered.

scope-cidr|A|A3|crest|Scope permits 192.0.2.0/28. A discovered backend is 192.0.2.18. What follows?|It is outside that prefix and needs separate scope treatment|It is included because the first three octets match|It is included because one application references it|It is included because it uses a familiar default port|The /28 covers .0 through .15. Architectural relevance is a lead, not an automatic expansion of authority.|Apply the exact boundary rather than a classful assumption.

scope-redirect|A|A3|crest|An approved URL redirects to a separately owned service. What should a tester do before testing the new service?|Resolve whether the redirected service is covered|Treat the redirect as complete authorization|Assume the services share all data and privileges|Expand to every domain in the destination's certificate|Routing behavior reveals a dependency. Scope must identify which parties and services are permitted.|Following application behavior can cross an ownership boundary.

test-window|A|A3|crest|A low-impact method is allowed only during a maintenance window. Does low expected impact remove that timing constraint?|No; the agreed window still applies|Yes; only destructive tests have timing constraints|Yes; a public asset has no timing conditions|No; the method becomes illegal everywhere permanently|Rules can constrain timing independently of expected technical impact. Use the agreed schedule and escalation path.|Authorization can have several simultaneous conditions.

credentials-scope|A|A3|crest|A provided account also works on an unlisted system. What does the successful login prove about test scope?|Nothing by itself about authorization for that system|The system automatically becomes in scope|The account may be used on every trusted host|The account's password grants supplier-wide approval|Credential capability and approved authority are distinct. Preserve the discovery as a lead and resolve the boundary.|Possession of a working credential is not a scope grant.

black-box-assumption|A|A1|crest|A black-box test finds no login endpoint. Which report statement is strongest?|No login endpoint was identified within the examined paths|The application has no authentication anywhere|Every hidden endpoint is unauthenticated|The application contains no confidential data|Describe observed coverage and collection limits. Absence from one discovery view is not a universal architecture conclusion.|Negative results need a bounded statement.

white-box-runtime|A|A1|crest|Source review finds a security check, but the deployed build is unknown. What remains to establish?|That the assessed deployment contains and applies that check|That all users have read the source|That the server uses exactly one IP address|That the application never changes state|A source snapshot can differ from runtime code/configuration. Bind evidence to the deployment being assessed.|Source presence is not deployed enforcement.

gray-box-role|A|A1|crest|A test includes one normal user account but no source or admin access. What assessment feature does this provide?|An authenticated perspective with limited internal information|A complete white-box view of every component|A guarantee that privilege escalation is permitted|A replacement for all unauthenticated discovery|Provided access defines one testing perspective. Further roles and source visibility remain distinct coverage dimensions.|A label such as gray-box does not define every permission.

retest-definition|A|A1|crest|A client requests a remediation retest. What should be agreed before testing?|The fixes, affected versions, cases, and expected closure criteria|Only the old report's filename|A guarantee that no new finding can exist|A requirement to repeat every historical action blindly|A retest verifies named changes and relevant regressions in an identified deployment. It is not automatically a complete new assessment.|Retest scope should define what closure means.

change-during-test|A|A3|crest|The client deploys a new application build mid-assessment. What should records distinguish?|Findings and tests associated with each build/state|Only the original test start date|Only the newest visible logo|A single timeless conclusion for both builds|A material change can alter behavior and applicability. Capture the transition and adapt coverage explicitly.|Evidence is tied to a system state.

limited-time|A|A3|crest|There is time for either repeated negative probes or testing an unexamined critical workflow. What should prioritization consider?|Client risk objectives, remaining coverage, and expected information gain|Only which tool produces the longest output|Only which endpoint has the shortest URL|Only the first scan's ordering|A bounded test needs deliberate prioritization. Additional repetition should resolve uncertainty rather than consume time without a purpose.|More traffic is not always more information.

resource-auth|A|A3|crest|An application has customer, support, and administrator roles. Why budget time for each perspective?|Each role exposes different reachable actions and boundaries|Every role necessarily sees identical permissions|Only the administrator's password strength matters|The number of roles determines the TLS key length|Role-based coverage can uncover horizontal and vertical authorization errors missed by one account.|Coverage is a matrix of identities and actions.

scope-api|A|A3|crest|A quote covers only the public website, but the mobile app uses a separate API. What should be clarified?|Whether API assets and workflows are part of the deliverable|Only the mobile app's icon dimensions|Only the customer's mail exchanger|Whether the website can use a darker theme|An application can have several interfaces to the same business process. Specify assets and interfaces rather than relying on an ambiguous product name.|A business system may have more than one technical entry point.

internal-external|A|A3|crest|Why distinguish internal and external infrastructure assessment positions?|Their routes, trust assumptions, and accessible services differ|Internal tests cannot identify vulnerabilities|External tests automatically include every private subnet|Both positions necessarily produce identical port states|A vantage point changes observed exposure and plausible attack paths. Report which position supports each conclusion.|Reachability is contextual.

scope-physical|A|A3|crest|The agreed engagement is a remote web test. A social-engineering opportunity is discovered. What is the appropriate scope treatment?|Record the lead and resolve separate authorization if relevant|Use it immediately because the goal is security|Treat every physical site as part of the web domain|Send the client's employees test messages without a stated scope|Different methods can impose different organizational risks. The contract's method boundary still matters.|A useful technique may be outside the agreed method set.

cleanup-ownership|A|A5|crest|Several files already exist on a host before testing. Which cleanup rule is most defensible?|Remove only identified test-owned artifacts under the agreed plan|Delete every suspicious-looking file|Delete the whole temporary directory regardless of ownership|Retain every newly created account indefinitely|Cleanup needs provenance and expected prior state. Existing or third-party artifacts should not be conflated with the test's changes.|Ownership must be known before deleting evidence or state.

cleanup-validation|A|A5|crest|An artifact-removal command returns success. What supports a defensible cleanup claim?|A follow-up check that the intended test artifact/state is gone|Only the command's printed word success|Only the tester's memory of the file path|Only a newer screenshot of an unrelated endpoint|Confirm the intended outcome and any residual effects. Tool return status is evidence of execution, not complete reversion.|Verify state rather than inferring it from an action receipt.

read-only-limit|A|A4|crest|An agreed read-only test finds an endpoint that may change records. What should the next discriminator prioritize?|A non-mutating way to assess the condition or an agreed change in test allowance|Changing a production record to see whether it works|Deleting a record so the impact is visible|Assuming the endpoint is harmless without any documentation|Respect the stated constraint while collecting useful evidence. A test plan can explicitly resolve a needed state-changing validation.|A promising lead does not cancel operational constraints.

production-copy|A|A4|crest|A destructive proof is run successfully on a staging copy. What must a production finding state?|The copy's relationship to production and the validation limit|That production was definitely compromised by the same test|That staging evidence can never be relevant|That every environmental difference is irrelevant|Comparable configuration can support a strong inference. Distinguish observed copy behavior from untested production consequences.|A representative environment is not the same environment.

lockout-stop|A|A4|crest|A credential test unexpectedly locks an authorized account. What should the immediate response follow?|The agreed stop, escalation, and recovery procedure|A wider spray to determine which other users lock|A silent password reset using any available privilege|A claim that lockouts were impossible under the scope|Unexpected disruption changes the operational condition. Preserve evidence and coordinate recovery instead of amplifying it.|A plan must handle risk actually materializing.

fragile-device|A|A4|crest|A device is known to fail under some malformed requests. Which approach best reduces assessment-introduced risk?|Use bounded approved checks and a recovery-aware test plan|Run the largest fuzzing corpus first|Assume the client accepted unlimited downtime|Skip documentation because the device is old|Select tests around objectives and operational tolerance. Known fragility warrants a specific method and rollback discussion.|Old or fragile systems require more precise discriminators.

new-compromise|A|A4|crest|A live test uncovers evidence of an unrelated attacker. Why may testing need to pause?|It could interfere with incident evidence or response|The tester now owns the incident investigation automatically|Every finding must immediately be published publicly|The original scope now authorizes retaliation|Use the agreed contact and preserve observations. Incident response and the penetration test may have different owners and scopes.|A discovered incident is not automatic incident-response authority.

likelihood-impact|A|A4|crest|A flaw is easy to exploit but reaches only non-sensitive disposable data. How should risk reasoning respond?|Consider exploitability and consequence separately|Assign maximum business impact solely from ease of exploitation|Assume low technical complexity means no risk|Replace evidence with a product popularity score|Likelihood and impact are distinct dimensions. Context matters without denying the underlying technical weakness.|One striking metric is not a full risk assessment.

technical-business|A|A4|crest|Two deployments share the same software flaw but hold different data and exposure. What may reasonably differ?|Their contextual business risk|The vulnerability's underlying mechanism necessarily|The hash length of every stored password|The definition of unauthorized access|Technical findings can have different practical consequences in different environments. Document the context supporting the rating.|Same defect does not require identical business consequence.

chain-risk|A|A4|crest|A low-privilege secret leak enables access to a more sensitive system. What should reporting connect?|The evidence-supported attack chain and its prerequisites|Only the first artifact's file size|A maximum severity without explaining the path|The unrelated systems' brand names alone|Business consequence can depend on combined weaknesses. Show the transitions and conditions rather than silently aggregating severity.|A chain needs evidence at its edges.

control-number|A|A4|crest|A finding maps to several control requirements. Does the number of mappings determine severity?|No; technical and business evidence determine the risk assessment|Yes; each mapping adds one severity level|Yes; three mappings always mean critical|No; control mappings make the finding irrelevant|Control applicability helps organize remediation/compliance discussion. It does not substitute for likelihood and consequence.|Compliance context should not inflate an unsupported risk claim.

false-positive|A|A5|crest|A scanner flags a vulnerability but a controlled check shows the relevant feature is absent. What should the report do?|Resolve or qualify the candidate using the contradictory evidence|Publish the scanner rating without qualification|Claim all scanners are unreliable everywhere|Ignore the feature check because it used fewer requests|Tool output is a candidate observation. Corroborating evidence determines whether the condition applies.|The report owns the conclusion, not the tool's label.

false-negative|A|A5|crest|An automated scan finds nothing, but a manual role test exposes another user's data. What follows?|The scan did not cover or detect that tested weakness|The manual result must be discarded|The application is secure because the scan passed|The flaw can only be a network firewall issue|Negative automated output does not override reproducible application evidence. Describe what the tool could and could not assess.|One testing method has a detection boundary.

sample-limit|A|A5|crest|Five of fifty endpoints were tested in depth. Which coverage statement is accurate?|Deep validation covered those five; other endpoints remain outside that depth|All fifty endpoints passed the same checks|The test found every possible authorization defect|Sampling proves the remaining endpoints are equivalent|State both the sampled surface and the reasons/limits of extrapolation. Untested paths are not passed paths.|Coverage claims should match performed work.

unreachable|A|A5|crest|A target times out from the tester's route. What should the result be called?|An unresolved reachability or response condition from that position|Proof that the host contains no services|Proof that the asset is permanently offline|Proof that all vulnerabilities were remediated|Record route, timing, method, and observed failure. An absent reply can have several causes.|No response is not a security pass.

negative-control|A|A5|crest|Why include a known-negative input when validating a suspected flaw?|Distinguish the alleged mechanism from generic behavior|Increase the total count of reported findings|Guarantee the target cannot log the test|Automatically prove business impact|A comparison helps identify whether a response follows the hypothesized condition rather than a catch-all or unrelated variation.|A discriminator needs a meaningful alternative outcome.

evidence-identity|A|A5|crest|Why record the authenticated principal in an authorization finding?|Access behavior depends on the caller's authority|The principal's name proves its password is strong|Every request is anonymous once stored in a report|Only TLS certificates determine user rights|The same operation can be valid for one role and improper for another. Preserve the role/account context.|A response without caller context can be ambiguous.

evidence-state|A|A5|crest|A bug depends on a workflow step performed earlier. What must reproduction retain?|The prerequisite state and ordering of steps|Only the final HTTP status code|Only the database product's logo|Only the last request's URL length|Stateful conditions can change outcomes. Specify setup, transitions, and expected observable results.|The final request may not be a standalone reproducer.

timestamp|A|A5|crest|Why retain timestamps for a test and its response?|Correlate observations with logs, builds, and system state|Guarantee the response content is cryptographically authentic|Replace the caller's role information|Automatically calculate every severity score|Timing supports provenance and troubleshooting, but does not by itself authenticate artifacts.|Time is context rather than proof of every claim.

prose-raw|A|A5|crest|Why keep relevant raw requests alongside an interpreted finding?|Readers can check whether evidence supports the interpretation|Raw traffic removes the need for a clear explanation|Every packet automatically becomes a critical finding|A screenshot can never supplement raw evidence|Raw artifacts and narrative serve different purposes. Explain which observations establish the claimed mechanism.|Evidence and interpretation should remain traceable.

repro-redaction|A|A5|ico|How can a report preserve reproduction value while limiting personal data exposure?|Use minimal representative evidence and document protected details appropriately|Remove all technical context from every finding|Publish the entire customer database in the appendix|Replace every observable response with a severity adjective|Retain what a reviewer needs to understand the cause, while limiting unrelated sensitive content and access.|Minimization should not erase the causal explanation.

finding-title|A|A5|crest|Which title best conveys a validated cross-account invoice read?|Customer can retrieve another customer's invoice|Critical vulnerability in the application|Tool warning number 17|The site has many query parameters|A concrete title identifies who can do what to which resource. Detail and limits belong in the body.|Specific behavior is more informative than an unexplained label.

remediation-root|A|A5|crest|A flaw allows unauthorized object access despite random IDs. Which recommendation addresses the cause?|Enforce object authorization for the caller|Add more random characters to IDs only|Change the page's visible button text only|Move the endpoint to a less obvious path only|Unpredictable identifiers can reduce discovery but do not establish access permission. Remediate the missing decision.|Obscurity should not replace the root control.

remediation-actionable|A|A5|crest|What makes remediation advice actionable for an engineering owner?|It identifies the failed control and where to enforce it|It says only use better security|It lists unrelated products without an implementation goal|It repeats the severity rating several times|Advice should connect the observed cause to a concrete control and verification expectation.|A slogan is not a repair plan.

retest-result|A|A5|crest|A patched endpoint blocks the original payload but an equivalent path still works. What is the retest outcome?|The original symptom changed but the flaw is not fully remediated|The finding is closed because one string was blocked|Every related endpoint must now be safe|The remaining path is irrelevant because it uses a different parameter|Retest the mechanism and affected scope, not merely a remembered payload string.|A root-cause fix must survive meaningful variants.

report-assumption|A|A5|crest|A report assumes a compromised host holds regulated data without evidence. How should this be handled?|Identify the assumption and seek or bound the supporting context|Present it as an observed data breach|Delete all technical evidence instead|Increase severity because the assumption sounds plausible|Business impact needs context. State which facts are known, inferred, or unresolved.|A plausible consequence is not an observed incident.

technical-reader|A|A5|crest|Which detail chiefly helps a technical owner reproduce a bug?|Exact conditions, inputs, identity, and observed output|Only a business-impact slogan|Only the count of scanners used|Only the engagement's invoice number|Technical reproduction needs the causal setup. Business-facing summaries can be concise without removing supporting detail.|Match information depth to the reader's task.

urgent-interim|A|A5|crest|A serious exposure is validated early in a long assessment. What purpose can an interim report serve?|Enable timely response while preserving final reporting accuracy|Declare the whole assessment complete automatically|Remove the need to retain evidence|Expand the tester's permissions without agreement|Interim communication can accelerate action and clarify operational decisions. Maintain provenance and update the final state.|Early notification and final closure are separate deliverables.

finding-duplicate|A|A5|crest|The same root control flaw affects several paths. What can a coherent report do?|Group the cause while listing affected cases and exceptions|Discard all but one affected path's existence|Invent a different cause for every URL|Count each response as an independent business breach|Grouping can make remediation clear without hiding breadth. Preserve distinct evidence and affected scope.|Consolidating presentation must not erase exposure information.

scope-budget-change|A|A3|crest|New discoveries double the asset list during a fixed-time test. What should be revisited?|Coverage priorities and agreed scope/time expectations|Only the final report's font size|Only the tester's favorite port-scanner flags|A promise to finish every original and new path at identical depth|Changes can affect effort and objectives. Communicate what can be covered rather than silently widening guarantees.|Discovery should inform explicit resource tradeoffs.

shared-production|A|A3|crest|A staging service shares its database with production. Why is that relevant to scoping?|A staging test can affect production data or behavior|The staging hostname guarantees independent risk|Production is unaffected whenever the UI looks different|Every staging account has no write permissions|Dependencies can cross environment labels. Establish actual shared state and permitted operations.|A deployment label is not a physical or data boundary.

third-party-logging|A|A3|ico|A testing service would send client request data to a third-party analyzer. What must be established?|Agreed data handling and permitted external processing|Only that the analyzer's interface is attractive|Only that the target is reachable publicly|That all captured data is automatically public|Handling rules and provenance apply to client/program information even when a testing tool offers convenient analysis.|Tool convenience does not define data-sharing permission.

evidence-retention|A|A5|ico|Why agree an evidence-retention period?|Limit unnecessary continued possession while supporting the engagement|Guarantee the report never needs correction|Make every captured secret permanent training data|Avoid keeping any proof of performed tests|Retention balances accountability, verification needs, and storage limitation. Apply the agreed protection and disposal plan.|Useful evidence need not be retained indefinitely.

data-purpose|A|A2|ico|A staff record was accessed to demonstrate excessive read access. Which later use is a different processing purpose?|Using it in unrelated marketing analysis|Using minimal protected proof in the agreed finding|Explaining the affected authorization rule|Recording the test's timing and role|Permission and lawful handling for assessment do not automatically extend to unrelated reuse. Purpose limitation matters.|An authorized collection can still have restricted later uses.

data-minimization|A|A2|ico|Which choice best demonstrates data minimization when one record proves a flaw?|Collect only the necessary representative evidence|Export every reachable record for future practice|Capture all unrelated attachments as background|Retain every customer's full profile automatically|Limit collection to the purpose and evidence need. Bigger captures can add risk without improving proof.|More bytes are not necessarily stronger evidence.

privacy-correspondence|A|A2|hra|Which type of information is within Article 8's protected privacy/correspondence interests?|Private email correspondence|Only publicly advertised product prices|Only a public software license title|Only a network protocol's published port assignment|Article 8 concerns private/family life, home, and correspondence. Applying legal duties requires the actual context and relevant framework.|Privacy interests can apply to communications as well as databases.

authorization-boundary|A|A2|cma|Why document allowed actions as well as target names?|Access can be authorized only for specified purposes or methods|A target name always authorizes every possible action|Only geography determines permitted methods|Documented actions automatically permit future unrelated tests|Authorization has scope and conditions. Intentional access outside granted authority can still raise misuse issues.|Permission is not merely an address list.

dual-use|A|A2|cma|Why is a tool's capability insufficient alone to classify every possession as computer misuse?|Legitimate purpose and the relevant legal elements matter|Any powerful tool is prohibited in every context|Only the tool's filename determines intent|Every downloaded script carries automatic legal permission|Dual-use tools can support legitimate testing or wrongdoing. The specific offense and circumstances determine the legal analysis.|Technical power is not the whole legal test.

payment-cvv|A|A2|pci|An ordinary merchant stores CVV after authorization, encrypted at rest. What is the PCI concern?|Encryption does not make that prohibited retention acceptable|Any encryption makes all payment data retention acceptable|CVV is only the cardholder's public username|PCI applies only to unencrypted network packets|PCI SSC explains that card verification values must not be stored after authorization by merchants, even encrypted.|Data-category restrictions can be stricter than an encryption requirement.

compliance-test|A|A2|crest|Why does a penetration test not by itself establish full compliance with a security standard?|The standard can require controls and evidence beyond the assessed tests|Compliance is determined only by the number of exploits|A clean scan certifies every organizational process|All regulations require identical test scopes|An assessment contributes evidence within its scope. Compliance encompasses applicable requirements and their assurance criteria.|Technical testing is one source of assurance evidence.

risk-transfer-limit|A|A4|crest|A client buys cyber insurance but leaves a public exploitable service unchanged. What distinction matters?|Financial risk treatment and technical exposure remain different|Insurance patches the service automatically|Transferred risk means the flaw no longer exists|Insurance makes data breaches technically impossible|Insurance can redistribute consequences. Exposure and control effectiveness still need evaluation.|A commercial treatment is not a technical fix.

risk-accept-owner|A|A4|crest|Who should own the decision to accept a documented residual business risk?|The appropriate authorized business risk owner|The scanner's default configuration|The attacker described in the finding|The nearest network switch|The assessor supplies evidence and recommendations; acceptance is a governance decision for the authorized owner.|Evidence ownership and risk-acceptance authority differ.

risk-avoid|A|A4|crest|A client retires an unnecessary exposed service entirely. Which treatment is most directly illustrated?|Avoidance of that activity's exposure|Transfer through insurance|Acceptance without changing the system|Only cosmetic reduction of the report severity|Removing an unneeded activity can avoid its associated exposure. Evaluate any dependencies and remaining services separately.|Avoiding one risk does not prove all related risks vanish.

protective-change|A|A4|crest|A firewall rule narrows who can reach a vulnerable service. What should a finding distinguish?|Reduced exposure from removal of the software flaw|That the code defect was necessarily repaired|That all insiders are unable to reach it|That every application credential is now stronger|A compensating restriction can reduce likelihood while leaving the vulnerability present for allowed or alternate paths.|A mitigation and a root-cause fix can be different states.

time-boxed-risk|A|A4|crest|A dangerous validation would consume the recovery window available to the client. What planning factor is missing?|Time for stabilization and rollback|Only the count of HTTP headers|Only the scanner's output theme|Only the test's narrative title|A testing window should allow both the experiment and recovery. Bound steps around realistic operational constraints.|A window is not entirely available for sending test traffic.

report-version|A|A5|crest|A finding is corrected after an initial draft. What makes the final deliverable clear?|A controlled final version with the corrected conclusion and evidence|Leaving contradictory drafts without marking their status|Adding a second severity without resolving the first|Removing dates from every artifact|Versioning and resolved conclusions help readers know which result governs. Retained drafts can be clearly historical.|A report should have an identifiable current conclusion.

evidence-integrity|A|A5|hash|Why hash a retained evidence artifact at capture time?|Support later checks that its bytes have not changed|Authenticate the target's every statement automatically|Prove the artifact contains no secret|Encrypt the artifact for every reviewer|A hash pins content bytes when the reference itself is trusted. Provenance and storage access are separate requirements.|Content integrity alone does not establish origin or confidentiality.

impact-limits|A|A5|crest|A tester reads one other user's invoice but does not test writes. Which claim is defensible?|Cross-user read access is demonstrated; write access is untested|Every user's invoice can be deleted|The database has been fully taken over|The finding has no impact because writes were not tried|State the specific action and context proved. Further privileges are separate hypotheses.|Demonstrated read impact should not be inflated to untested control.

handover|A|A1|crest|What should a technical handover include so another assessor can continue accurately?|Current evidence, scope, unresolved questions, and completed negative tests|Only a preferred attack name|Only a list of successful screenshots|Only the next person's favorite tool|A successor needs both confirmed state and limits, including falsified paths. This avoids duplicated work and unsupported assumptions.|Useful continuity includes negative evidence.

coverage-versus-volume|A|A5|crest|A run sends ten thousand requests to one endpoint. What does request volume alone establish about breadth?|Little without the tested behaviors and surfaces|Complete application coverage|Validation of every user role|Absence of all client-side bugs|Volume may reflect repetition. Coverage requires distinct assets, states, identities, and mechanisms assessed.|Breadth is about exposure to meaningful cases, not only traffic count.

scope-renewal|A|A3|crest|An old authorization expires before a planned retest. What needs resolution?|Current authority for the retest's dates and actions|Only whether the old report is still readable|Only whether the hostname still resolves|Automatic use of any account from the earlier test|Authority can be time-limited and environment-specific. Establish the current agreement rather than inheriting an expired one.|Historical permission is not necessarily current permission.

closure-open-item|A|A1|crest|One critical workflow could not be assessed because required access was unavailable. How should closure describe it?|An explicit coverage limit or unresolved item|A passed workflow because no flaw was observed|A confirmed vulnerability without any evidence|A completed test hidden from the client|Unperformed work remains a limitation, even when the rest of the engagement concludes. Explain its consequence for assurance.|Completion of an engagement is not proof every planned case was assessed.
